svg.text: Formal Verification (Module 3a) — Scyther v1.3.0, --max-runs=4
32 claims verified · 8 failing BY DESIGN · one real bug found that the simulator could not see
register.spdl — 8/8 ✓
1. V→TA V,{TagCertReq,V,pid,EMS,nv}k(V,TA)
2. TA→V {TagCert,pid,EMS,V,nv}sk(TA)
roles: V, TA · claims: Alive, Weakagree, Niagree, Nisynch
k(V,TA) is the provisioning credential — without it the
model would describe a TA issuing EMS certs to anyone,
which would make the whole defence vacuous.
priority.spdl — THE LOAD-BEARING MODEL
3. V→C V,{TagCert,pid,EMS,V}sk(TA),nv,
{TagAssert,V,pid,EMS,nv,C}sk(V)
4. C→V {TagGrant,nv,nc,V,C}sk(C)
claim_C4(C, Nisynch) = Ok, proof of correctness
the assertion binds the TARGET HEAD C, so an assertion
overheard in one cluster cannot be relayed into another
What C4 establishes
Nisynch over 3 roles requires EVERY preceding event in
EVERY role to have a matching partner, in order. So a
head's slot grant implies:
• a REAL TA run issued that role to that vehicle
• a REAL vehicle run asserted it
• all three agree on pid, role, nonce
• the nonce rules out replay
aggregate.spdl — 12/12 ✓ (three deployed message types)
chirp-member M→C {TagReading, M,reading,nm,C}k(M,C)
chirp-aggregate C→R {TagAggregate, C,agg,nc,R}k(C,R)
chirp-verbatim V→R {TagEmergency, V,pid,EMS,emsg,nv,R}sk(V)
chirp-verbatim R.Nisynch: the RSU authenticates the VEHICLE
end-to-end, through a relay it does not trust at all.
fusion-limit.spdl — 0/2, FAILS BY DESIGN
Can the RSU authenticate the MEMBER through a fused packet?
R.Niagree and R.Nisynch both FAIL. That failure IS the result.
The fused value is fresh at the head, not a recoverable function
of the readings. A MAC attests to WHO SENT a value, never to
whether it faithfully summarises anything.
→ a compromised head can fabricate it, undetectably.
THE BUG SCYTHER FOUND — cross-protocol MAC confusion
Before (no domain separation) — the two data-path MACs were structurally identical:
member reading : {M, reading, nm, C}k(M,C)
fused aggregate : {C, agg, nc, R}k(C,R)
Attack trace (verbatim from --dot-output):
Run#2 Alice as HEAD, chirp-AGGREGATE → RSU Charlie:
(Alice,agg,nc,{Alice,agg,nc,Charlie}k(Alice,Charlie))
Run#1 Charlie accepts the SAME bitstring as a MEMBER READING.
Failure signature — and why it is diagnostic
Alive and Weakagree PASSED; Niagree and Nisynch FAILED.
The receiver had the right peer but the WRONG MESSAGE MEANING.
Fix + re-verification
A distinct constant tag inside every MAC and signature, so the
message types occupy disjoint formats. All 12 claims then verify,
and the suite verifies identically file-by-file OR concatenated.
Why the simulator could never find this
In network.py a member reading and a fused aggregate are DIFFERENT
PYTHON VARIABLES reached by different code paths. There is no
bitstring and no wire format, so the confusion cannot be represented.
The simulator cannot express the bug. This is the argument for doing formal work.
And the architectural payoff of fusion-limit.spdl
Because a class-2 message is never transformed, the vehicle's own
signature survives the relay to the RSU. So the bypass gains a SECOND
justification with nothing to do with latency:
Fusion buys energy and costs provenance.
The six failing claims in priority.spdl are NOT a vulnerability — diagnosed by experiment, after two wrong guesses
Cause: the TA never learns which cluster head the vehicle will later talk to. Registration happens offline and once; message 1 carries no head identity.
Weakagree over three roles asks whether EVERY other role is "running the protocol with" the claimer — and the TA is not running with any head.
Confirmed: delete the TA role, keep the exchange identical, and all six verify → preserved as priority-assert.spdl (8/8 ✓).
Rejected first: (a) "no adversary action" — the trace did contain a redirect node; (b) "the signature doesn't bind V" — binding V changed nothing.
